answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every identity to lock a refundable stake before it earns rewards, like a cedar post sunk deep before a fence holds. The work of each agent is then attested by peers, and a proven fake or duplicate forfeits its bond, so spinning up thousands of sock-puppets costs real capital instead of free keystrokes. Honest agents keep their opal-bright reputation and their stake, while a juniper hedge of random peer audits catches copies early, making mass fakery unprofitable.
